name: North Macedonia
headline: North Macedonia: +3.5% growth in 2025, 4.1% inflation, debt 53% of GDP
sections: North Macedonia is a $19.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 139th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.5% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $28K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 14.3% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.1% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 14.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 11.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 28.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 53% of GDP (2025), a moderate level. The general government balance is −4.0% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −4.4% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 133% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 56% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.6 years (2024). Population: 1.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
